title: zazzle-csharp-indexer code-question use case
description: How a coding agent's question about the code reaches the index and comes back.

entities.name: Answer a question about the code
entities.description: A coding agent asks zazzle-csharp-indexer, through its MCP client, where something is, what a file contains or what matches a pattern.
entities.goal: Get a compact, current answer about the code in its work tree, such as its structure, where a symbol is declared or used, or what changed.
preconditions: The agent's MCP client is configured to start zazzle-csharp-indexer serve, by zazzle-csharp-indexer init or by hand.
Every root is inside a git work tree, and git is on PATH.
postconditions: The agent has the answer as text, or a tool error it can act on.
The call is in the usage log, with how the answer was produced.

flow.action: Its MCP client starts zazzle-csharp-indexer serve, with --root arguments or in the project directory.
Connects to the daemon socket in the state directory, starting the daemon when nothing answers, and sends its version and roots.
Checks each root is inside a git work tree and attaches its index, starting the watcher and the initial reconcile the first time the root is seen; replies ok.

Initializes the MCP session and lists the tools, receiving the instructions to read, search and edit files through zazzle and to use these tools for C# structure (overview, find_symbol, find_references, changed_since, git_log, git_blame).
Calls a tool, for example search with a pattern or read with root:path and a line range.
The tool waits for the index, re-checks the files it will use, answers from the index and the files under a token budget, and the server logs the call.
Pages on with offset or start_line, or reads what it found; if the tools cannot answer, it may say so with report_gap and fall back to run, as those tools' descriptions invite.

alternatives.outcome: serve opens its own engine and answers in process.

alternatives.condition: The daemon runs another version and has no other clients.
alternatives.outcome: It stops; serve starts a new one and tries again (three attempts in all).

alternatives.condition: No daemon starts within five seconds, or one of another version is still serving other clients.
alternatives.outcome: serve notes it on standard error and answers in process.

alternatives.condition: A root is not a directory or not inside a git work tree.
alternatives.outcome: The daemon refuses the session; serve falls back to in process, where the same check stops it with the error.

alternatives.condition: The index is still building after the 30-second ready timeout.
alternatives.outcome: search and find_files answer from a plain git listing; overview, find_symbol and find_references return index_cold.

alternatives.condition: The tool fails (bad arguments, path outside the root, unknown root, git error, refused command).
alternatives.outcome: The agent gets a result with isError true and the message; the log records the error code.
